console-bg.purpose: The desk: body background, agent text and dispatch lines sit directly on it.

console-fg.purpose: Foreground on the console; desk-strip title is ink, this is the desk's own text.

console-surface.purpose: Printer bar, choice buttons, kbd, the HeroUI surface layer.

console-surface-secondary.purpose: Markdown table headers and help-dialog code chips.

console-muted.purpose: Time gutter, speaker labels, dispatch's ordinary voice.

console-border.purpose: 1px rules: printer top edge, code fences, table cells, blockquote bar.

console-field.purpose: Textarea and fenced-code background on the desk.

console-link.purpose: Links in agent Markdown and dispatch lines.

rack.purpose: The sidebar the strips sit in; grained with an 8px repeating rule.

rack-ink.purpose: Bay labels, the wordmark's 'strip board', ghost buttons on the rack.

rack-rule.purpose: 1px rule running from a bay label to the rack's edge; the rack footer's top edge.

paper-buff.purpose: Default strip, slip and desk strip: threads hosted by the web transport.

paper-blue.purpose: Strips hosted by Slack and slips written via Slack.

paper-amber.purpose: A waiting strip, the desk strip while waiting, an open prompt.

paper-pink.purpose: A failed strip and the desk strip of a failed thread.

paper-grey.purpose: A closed strip, a settled prompt; shadowless.

ink.purpose: Everything printed on paper: titles, values, links, stamps.

ink-2.purpose: Second line of a strip, field keys, settled prompt text, ages.

ink-rule.purpose: The dashed perforation on every strip; the dashed rule above a riding prompt.

flag-run-ink.purpose: The RUN flag's box and letters, on any paper.

flag-fail-ink.purpose: The FAIL flag's box and letters, on any paper.

lamp-wait.purpose: The lit, pulsing lamp of a strip that needs a human; the mark's lamp.

lamp-run.purpose: The lamp of a working thread, the live line, and the link indicator.

lamp-fail.purpose: The lamp of a failed thread and a dropped link.

lamp-off.purpose: The lamp every other state carries: ink at 18%, inset-shadowed.

accent.purpose: HeroUI accent: ALLOW, SEND, Sign in; the @mention callout in dispatch lines.

success.purpose: Dispatch lines beginning with a check mark.

warning.purpose: Dispatch lines beginning with pause/warn/stop/recycle glyphs.

danger.purpose: DENY button, failed dispatch lines, login/password errors.

focus.purpose: Focus ring on strips (2px outside a 2px console gap) and HeroUI fields.

headline.purpose: The pulled strip's title and the wordmark; 15px 600, one line.

title.purpose: A racked strip's title; 13px 500, 700 while unread.

body.purpose: Agent Markdown and human slips at 14px/1.55, 72ch measure.

sys.purpose: dispatch's own lines at 13px/1.45 in console-muted, 80ch.

data.purpose: Desk-strip field values, live line, riding prompt text, file names; mono 12px tabular.

gutter.purpose: The log's time column, strip second line and age, speaker line; mono 11px tabular.

label.purpose: Bay labels, speaker labels, @mention; mono 11px uppercase 0.06em. Field keys and form labels on paper drop to 10px at 0.1em.

flag.purpose: Four-letter flags, unread stamps, button faces; mono 10px uppercase 0.08em, 700 for WAIT and FAIL.

shadows.name: paper-shadow
shadows.purpose: Paper at rest: racked strips, slips, settled prompts, closed desk strip.

shadows.name: paper-shadow-up
shadows.purpose: Paper pulled: current strip, cocked waiting strip, desk strip, open prompt, toast.

shadows.name: lamp-glow-wait
shadows.purpose: Ring and glow on the amber lamp.

shadows.name: lamp-glow-run
shadows.purpose: Ring and glow on the green lamp.

shadows.name: lamp-glow-fail
shadows.purpose: Ring and glow on the red lamp.

motion.name: ease-paper
motion.purpose: Strip hover/cock transform and shadow (180ms); the pull-onto-desk animation (220ms).

motion.name: duration-pull
motion.purpose: Desk strip entering: translateY(-6px) and opacity 0.6 to rest.

motion.name: lamp-ask
motion.purpose: The waiting lamp's pulse; off under prefers-reduced-motion, as are the strip transitions.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Above: rack static at 19.5rem, time gutter shown. Below: rack slides in over a backdrop, time moves into the speaker line.

colorSchemes.source: internal/transport/web/ui/src/styles.css @layer base; .dark toggled by main.tsx from prefers-color-scheme
colorSchemes.note: Every colorMeta entry with a `dark` field is redefined under .dark; ink, ink-2, ink-rule, lamp-off, accent-foreground and danger-foreground are not, by the Paper Is Always Lit Rule.

mark.note: The favicon cannot read custom properties, so it carries fixed hex approximations of paper-buff, ink and lamp-wait.

sysTone.note: Tone is read off the glyph the coordinator already emits; the UI adds no glyphs of its own.

components.css: .ds-sheet{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:0.75rem;align-items:center;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);padding:0.75rem 1rem;border-radius:2px;box-shadow:var(--paper-shadow)}.ds-pair{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px}.ds-stamp{font-family:var(--font-strip,ui-monospace,'SF Mono',Menlo,Consolas,'DejaVu Sans Mono',monospace);font-size:10px;font-weight:700;line-height:1;padding:3px 5px 2px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--ink);color:var(--paper)}.ds-flag{font-family:var(--font-strip,ui-monospace,'SF Mono',Menlo,Consolas,monospace);font-size:10px;line-height:1;letter-spacing:0.08em;padding:3px 4px 2px 5px;border:1px solid currentColor;border-radius:2px;color:var(--ink-2);white-space:nowrap}.ds-flag[data-state=wait]{color:var(--ink);border-color:var(--ink);font-weight:700}.ds-flag[data-state=run]{color:oklch(0.4 0.12 150);border-color:oklch(0.4 0.12 150)}.ds-flag[data-state=fail]{color:oklch(0.48 0.19 27);border-color:oklch(0.48 0.19 27);font-weight:700}.ds-flag[data-state=closed]{border-style:dashed}.ds-lamp{display:inline-block;width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--lamp-off);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 1px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.25);flex:none}.ds-lamp[data-state=wait]{background:var(--lamp-wait);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px oklch(0.5 0.12 75 / 0.5),0 0 8px 2px oklch(0.8 0.17 75 / 0.55);animation:ds-lamp-ask 1.3s ease-in-out infinite}.ds-lamp[data-state=run]{background:var(--lamp-run);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px oklch(0.45 0.12 150 / 0.5),0 0 6px 1px oklch(0.76 0.18 150 / 0.45)}.ds-lamp[data-state=fail]{background:var(--lamp-fail);box-shadow:0 0 0 1px oklch(0.4 0.15 27 / 0.5),0 0 6px 1px oklch(0.66 0.22 27 / 0.45)}@keyframes ds-lamp-ask{0%,100%{filter:brightness(1)}50%{filter:brightness(0.7)}}

narrative.overview:
Every thread is a paper flight-progress strip. The operator reads a rack of printed strips down the left edge and pulls one onto the desk; the open strip sits across the head of the desk with its fields printed on it, the log runs beneath it in a time-gutter grid, and the printer (the composer) sits along the bottom. The console is brushed aluminium in daylight and graphite-blue at night; the paper is always light and the ink is always dark, whichever the scheme. State is carried by a lamp (amber asks, green runs, red failed) and a four-letter printed flag, never by colour alone, and a strip that needs a human is lit and cocked out of the rack so it is found without hunting.

The world refuses the chat-app scaffold: no avatars, no bubbles, no sidebar list of conversations. Instead the material says who is speaking. Humans write on paper (strips, slips, prompts); the machine speaks on the desk (agent Markdown, dispatch's own lines in the rack's muted voice). Density is high and quiet: an all-day second-monitor surface that earns trust by being legible from across the room and calm up close.

Type follows the same split. Anything printed on a strip or measured (flags, field values, elapsed times, the time gutter, labels, the live line) is set in the system monospace; prose (titles, agent text, dispatch's lines, help) is the system sans. No fonts are bundled.
keyCharacteristics: Paper on a console: warm buff and pale-blue strips lift off a cool grey-blue rack and desk.
Lamp plus flag for every state; only WAIT, RUN and FAIL light a lamp.
A cocked strip (translated 8px, rotated -0.4deg, lifted shadow) is the one dramatic gesture.
Mono for printed data, sans for prose; 10-15px, tabular numerals throughout.
Two shadows only: paper at rest, paper pulled.
2px corners on paper; perforated (dashed) left edge on every strip.

rules.name: The Lamp Rule
rules.body: State is a lamp plus a printed flag. Only WAIT, RUN and FAIL light a lamp (amber, green, red); every other state shows the unlit lamp and its four-letter flag. Colour is never the sole carrier.

rules.name: The Paper Is Always Lit Rule
rules.body: Paper stays light and ink stays dark in both colour schemes; the dark scheme darkens the console and the rack, lowers paper by ~0.03 L, and leaves every `ink` token untouched.

rules.name: The Paper/Desk Rule
rules.body: What a human writes or must answer is printed on paper; what the machine says sits on the desk. Agent Markdown and dispatch's own lines never get a paper background.

rules.name: The Host Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue paper means Slack hosts or wrote it; buff means the web. The host colour yields to state: a waiting strip is amber and a failed strip is pink whoever hosts it.

rules.name: The Printed Data Rule
rules.body: If it is a value a controller reads off a strip (flag, field, time, count, tool name), it is mono with tabular numerals. If it is a sentence, it is sans.

rules.name: The Four-Letter Flag Rule
rules.body: A state is printed as exactly four uppercase letters in a 1px box: WAIT RUN FAIL CLSD DONE IDLE QUED INTR CNCL NEW. New states join this set; nothing else is boxed like a flag except the SIGN IN card's flag.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: Paper is at rest or pulled; there is no third elevation. A strip rises by changing shadow and translating 8px, never by scaling or adding a border.

rules.name: The Cocked Strip Rule
rules.body: A waiting strip is pulled 8px out of the rack and rotated -0.4deg (10px, no rotation, when it is also the current one). Hover nudges a strip 3px; nothing else on the board moves sideways.

dos: **Do** put a lamp and a four-letter flag on anything that has a state; light the lamp only for WAIT, RUN and FAIL.
**Do** print what humans write or must answer on paper (buff, blue for Slack, amber while asking, pink when failed, grey once settled or closed), and leave what the machine says on the desk.
**Do** keep paper light and ink dark in both colour schemes; change only the console, the rack and the shadows for dark.
**Do** set printed data (flags, fields, times, counts, tool names, button faces) in the system mono with tabular numerals, and prose in the system sans.
**Do** use the two paper shadows only: at rest for racked and settled paper, pulled for current, cocked, desk and open-prompt paper.
**Do** give every strip its perforated left edge (1px dashed `ink-rule`) and 2px corners.
**Do** keep the answer on the strip: while a thread waits, the open prompt's choices ride on the desk strip.
**Do** keep the ramp between 10px and 15px and measures at 72ch (prose on paper or agent text) and 80ch (dispatch lines).
donts: **Don't** draw avatars, chat bubbles, or a plain list of conversations; the rack of strips and the desk are the scaffold.
**Don't** let colour carry state alone; a tinted line or paper always has its lamp, flag, or leading glyph.
**Don't** give agent Markdown or dispatch's own lines a paper background or shadow.
**Don't** add a third elevation, a border-on-hover, or scale transforms; paper rises by shadow and an 8px translate only.
**Don't** round anything past 3px except HeroUI's 0.2rem controls and the 8px lamp; no pills.
**Don't** rotate anything except the cocked waiting strip (-0.4deg) and the decision stamp (-1.5deg).
**Don't** bundle a webfont or introduce a third family; the system sans and system mono stacks are the type.
**Don't** invent a state name that is not four uppercase letters, and don't print a flag without its box.
**Don't** let the blue host paper override a waiting (amber) or failed (pink) strip.
